SEARCH
Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor

Class SearchEngine

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.SearchEngine
public final class SearchEngine extends Object
The pure search-and-replace engine behind the editor's Find bar: literal or regular-expression matching, optional case sensitivity, forward/backward navigation with wrap-around, match counting and replace-one / replace-all.

Everything here works on plain Strings and never touches Swing, so the full semantics (including the regex edge cases) are unit-testable headless; the UI layer only maps offsets back onto the document. Literal queries are compiled with Pattern.quote(java.lang.String) and literal replacements escaped with Matcher.quoteReplacement(java.lang.String), so a user's $1 or ( is always taken at face value unless the regex toggle is on. An invalid regex surfaces as PatternSyntaxException from compile(java.lang.String, boolean, boolean) for the UI to report; a zero-length regex match advances one character so scanning can never livelock.

    • findAll

      public static List<SearchEngine.Match> findAll(String text, String query, boolean regex, boolean matchCase)
      Every match of query in text, in order, stopping at MAX_MATCHES. Returns an empty list for a null/empty query or an invalid regex (the UI validates separately through compile(java.lang.String, boolean, boolean)).

    • find

      public static SearchEngine.Match find(String text, String query, int from, boolean regex, boolean matchCase, boolean backward, boolean wrap)
      The next match at or after from (forward) or at or before it (backward), wrapping around the document when wrap is set. Returns null when nothing matches in the requested direction.

    • replaceAll

      public static SearchEngine.ReplaceResult replaceAll(String text, String query, String replacement, boolean regex, boolean matchCase)
      Replaces every match in one pass. In literal mode the replacement is inserted verbatim; in regex mode $n / ${name} group references and \ escapes are honoured, tolerantly: a dangling $ or a reference to a non-existent group is kept verbatim rather than failing the whole operation.

    • replaceOne

      public static String replaceOne(String text, SearchEngine.Match match, String replacement, String query, boolean regex, boolean matchCase)
      Replaces a single previously located match. The replacement goes through the same literal/regex group semantics as replaceAll(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String, boolean, boolean). A stale match (outside the text, or no longer matching the query at that offset) leaves the text unchanged.
